input: Clear and organize the garage storage shelves

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many shelving units or sections are involved changes the scale of the plan — a single shelf is a 1-hour job, while an entire wall of shelving could be a multi-day project.
Whether this is a solo effort or involves other household members affects task delegation, decision-making authority over items, and scheduling.
Understanding what categories of items are currently on the shelves (tools, sports gear, holiday decorations, etc.) determines the organizational system and labeling needed.
A hard deadline (e.g., hosting an event, selling the house) or time budget per session shapes how aggressively to tackle the project and whether to break it into phases.
Knowing what to do with items being removed — donate, trash, sell, or relocate — is the single most-blocking decision that determines what supplies and next steps are needed.
The desired organizational style (grouped by category, by frequency of use, by person, etc.) directly drives how items get sorted and placed back on the shelves.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — whether it's just tidy, or fully labeled with bins and a maintained system — sets the bar for effort and investment required.

gold.taskTitle: Clear and organize garage storage shelves
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to declutter and reorganize the items stored on their garage shelving units.

questions.title: How many shelving units or shelf sections are involved?
questions.description: Establishes the overall scale and scope of the project to determine if this is a single session or a multi-phase effort.

questions.title: Will you be doing this alone or with others?
questions.description: Determines whether tasks can be delegated and whether others need to weigh in on decisions about shared items.

questions.title: What types of items are currently stored on the shelves?
questions.description: Identifies the categories of items (tools, seasonal decor, sports equipment, etc.) to plan an appropriate organizational system.

questions.title: Do you have a target date to finish this project?
questions.description: A hard deadline or preferred completion window shapes how the work is broken into sessions and how quickly decisions need to be made.

questions.title: What will happen to items you decide to remove?
questions.description: Clarifies whether removed items will be donated, trashed, sold, or moved elsewhere, which determines what supplies and follow-up steps are needed.

questions.title: How do you want items grouped once reorganized?
questions.description: Defines the preferred sorting logic — by category, by user, by frequency of use — which drives the entire layout of the shelves.

questions.title: What does a fully successful result look like to you?
questions.description: Distinguishes between a basic tidy-up versus a fully labeled, bin-organized, long-term maintainable system, setting the right level of effort and investment.
